info.title: FTS Studio API
info.description: Access FinTech Studios intelligence platform via API. Search across multiple news sources, generate AI-powered executive summaries, manage collections, access insight channels, and more.

post.description: Search for news articles across multiple sources (FTS, NewsAPI, Brave). Returns deduplicated articles sorted by date with original source URLs. Credits are charged dynamically per source queried (FTS search cost, NewsAPI article_search cost, Brave web_search cost).

post.description:
Execute a collection's sources and return aggregated articles. Fetches from all configured sources, applies filters, merges, and deduplicates results.

**Execute is always date-bounded, never silently result-bounded.** The window is your `date_start`/`date_end` if given, else the collection's saved date range, else **the last 30 days**. The applied window comes back as `date_start`/`date_end`/`date_window_source`, so a default window is always visible rather than inferred. Results are ordered by `published_at` descending (newest first, `url` as tiebreaker) regardless of the collection's merge strategy.

**The result cap follows the same precedence as the window:** your `max_articles`, else the collection's stored `max_articles_per_refresh`, else unbounded — every article in the window. The FTS news source is our own API, so an unbounded execute pages through it, up to a hard ceiling of 5000 articles per query. A cap caps the window rather than replacing it, and it is pushed down to the sources, so `total_in_range` is bounded by it too: only an uncapped execute reports the true size of the window. Third-party sources (web search) keep their configured per-source limit and vendor caps either way.

There is no offset/cursor pagination — every execute re-fetches live, so there is no stable result set to page over. Two signals tell you the answer was cut short: `has_more` means your cap bit, and `truncated_sources` means a source hit its own ceiling with news still unread in the window. For the latter, split the window into calendar chunks that each stay under 5000 and merge the results — see `truncated_sources`.

max_articles.description: Ceiling on returned articles, applied within the window. Omit to fall back to the collection's stored max_articles_per_refresh, and if that is unset too, to every article in the window (no cap).

date_start.description: Inclusive lower bound on published_at. ISO-8601 UTC datetime, or a bare YYYY-MM-DD (widened to 00:00:00.000Z that day). Defaults to the collection's saved range, else 30 days ago.

date_end.description: Inclusive upper bound on published_at. Omit for 'up to now'. A bare YYYY-MM-DD is widened to 23:59:59.999Z that day.

post.description: Generate a chat completion using an LLM via OpenRouter. Supports multiple model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Perplexity). Credits charged dynamically based on token usage.

provider_params.description: Provider-specific request parameters forwarded to the upstream LLM via OpenRouter. Known Perplexity params: return_images (boolean), return_related_questions (boolean), search_recency_filter (string: 'month'|'week'|'day'|'hour'), search_domain_filter (string[]).

enrich_citations.description: When true, post-process provider metadata to extract a structured `citations` array as a sibling to `provider_metadata`. Currently resolves Perplexity citation URLs into objects with url, title, source_name, and date. Raw provider_metadata is never modified. Response content `[n]` references are preserved as-is for apps to render as they choose.

normalize_images.description: When true, normalize provider-specific image metadata into a consistent schema. Maps variant field names (image_url/url/src, origin_url/source_url/page_url) to stable fields: url, source_url, width, height, alt, source_domain. Deduplicates by URL. Raw provider_metadata.images is never modified.

provider_metadata.description: Raw provider-specific response metadata, passed through unmodified. Contents vary by provider. Perplexity models may return: citations (string[] of URLs), images (object[]), related_questions (string[]), search_results (object[]).

citations.description: Structured citation objects resolved from provider metadata. Only present when `enrich_citations: true` was set in the request AND the provider returned citation data. Content `[n]` references are NOT rewritten — apps decide how to render them using this array.

title.description: Article/page title from search results, if available

source_name.description: Short source name derived from title or URL hostname

date.description: Publication date from search results, if available

images.description: Normalized image objects from provider metadata. Only present when `normalize_images: true` was set in the request AND the provider returned image data. All provider-specific field name variants are mapped to a consistent schema. Deduplicated by URL.

source_url.description: URL of the page where the image was found

source_domain.description: Domain name of the source page (e.g. 'reuters.com')

post.description: Generate a streaming chat completion via Server-Sent Events. Same parameters as /chat/completions, including provider_params. Content chunks arrive as `choices[0].delta.content`. The final chunk includes `finish_reason: "stop"`, `usage`, and `provider_metadata` (if the upstream provider returns extra fields). Terminated by `data: [DONE]`.

provider_params.description: Provider-specific request parameters forwarded to the upstream LLM via OpenRouter. Known Perplexity params: return_images (boolean), return_related_questions (boolean), search_recency_filter (string: 'month'|'week'|'day'|'hour'), search_domain_filter (string[]).

enrich_citations.description: When true, the final SSE event includes a structured `citations` array resolved from provider metadata. See /chat/completions for full schema.

normalize_images.description: When true, the final SSE event includes a normalized `images` array. See /chat/completions for full schema.

200.description: SSE stream of chat completion chunks. Final chunk includes provider_metadata, usage, and optionally citations and images (when enrichment flags are set).

get.description: Returns the list of supported LLM models available for chat completions. Includes model capabilities, context windows, and tier requirements.

get.summary: Resolve an API key to its owner
get.description: Returns the identity of the Studio user that owns the presented API key. `user_id` is the Studio users.id — the same value POST /api/system/provision-app-key returns, and identical across every key belonging to that user. Not metered: no credits are charged and the call succeeds even for a user with no credit account. Unlike other v1 endpoints this authenticates by API key only — a session cookie will not satisfy it, because the endpoint's purpose is to identify the presented key.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days to look back

max_articles_per_refresh.description: Result cap this collection executes under when a request does not pass max_articles. Null means unbounded within the window.

date_start.description: Start of the window actually applied — your date_start, else the collection's saved range, else 30 days ago. Always present.

date_end.description: End of the window actually applied. Always present.

date_window_source.description: Where the applied window came from. `default` means neither you nor the collection specified one and the 30-day default was used.

total_in_range.description: Articles matching the window before max_articles was applied. Bounded by what the sources returned, so it is not a corpus total.

has_more.description: There is more news in this window than you received — because your max_articles bit, or because a source hit its own ceiling. Check truncated_sources to tell which.

truncated_sources.description:
Sources that stopped with articles still unread in this window. If a source appears here after an unbounded execute, it hit its own ceiling (FTS reaches 5000 per query) and the only way to see the rest is a narrower date range — raising max_articles will not help. Absent when nothing was truncated.

To cover a window that exceeds the ceiling, split it into calendar chunks that each stay under 5000 (month by month for a busy query, week by week for a very busy one), execute each chunk, and merge the results. Chunk until no chunk reports truncation and the coverage is complete — the article order within a chunk does not matter, because every chunk that comes back untruncated is exhaustive for its own dates.
